note: Files the template distributes to repos that `biffo core upgrade` cannot reach. Instances carry biffo.core.json and a core-manifest.json, so they are upgraded by the CLI's three-way merge. Sibling apps (biffo.sibling.json) and plugin repos (biffo.plugin.json) are SEPARATE REPOSITORIES with neither, and until 2026-07-29 the only documented channel to them was 'vendor into the skeleton, plus a one-time manual copy-in for existing ones'. That is not a mechanism, it is a hope: the skeleton only helps repos created afterwards, and nothing ever prompts the copy-in. It is how AGENTS.md drifted 68 lines behind in tabsii (#559), and how eight repos ended up running a local gate two versions old that checked one thing in eight (#855). scripts/shared-sync.sh reads this list, reports drift with --check, and opens a PR per repo without it. Add a file here only if every sibling and plugin should have the template's copy verbatim -- this is a one-way overwrite, not a merge, so nothing a repo is expected to customise belongs in it. Scope is any repo carrying one of `appliesTo`'s markers OR any repo that already holds scripts/verify.sh: the runner repos have neither marker but did receive the gate, and distributing a file once then losing track of it recreates the drift this exists to end. scripts/shared-sync.sh additionally writes .biffo-shared-version into each target -- the template core version the files came from, read from the TEMPLATE and never from the target, so it cannot report perfect health by comparing a repo to itself. The two dependency-audit scripts were added for #743: this repo hardened its own audits in #591/#592/#636/#717/#721 and both skeletons kept shipping the raw `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` / `uv run pip-audit`, so every satellite was born reddening a required check on any registry hiccup. They qualify as verbatim content because they take their target from the CI job's working directory rather than from a repo layout -- one byte-identical file is correct in this repo's root, in a sibling's apps/frontend and services/api, and in a plugin repo's root alike. js-dependency-audit.sh lands in Python-only plugin repos too and is simply never invoked there; that is the price of a one-way overwrite with no per-repo conditionals, and it is cheaper than the conditionals. The two destructive-plan scripts were added for #1123: the guard (#387) was wired into deploy-infra.yml and therefore reached INSTANCES only, while five sibling repos ran `terraform apply -auto-approve` with no plan stage, no guard and no copy of the script -- and the sibling skeleton had the same shape, so every sibling created afterwards was born without it. They qualify as verbatim content for the same reason the audits do: check-destructive-plan.mjs takes its plan file as an argument and resolves the module beside itself, so one byte-identical pair is correct at a repo root, in an instance, and in a sibling whose terraform lives under a `working-directory: infra` -- the workflow passes $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, so nothing in the script knows the layout. They have no dependencies and run on bare node, which is why they can execute in a Terraform job that installs no toolchain. Like js-dependency-audit.sh, they land in plugin repos that run no Terraform and are simply never invoked there. NOTE the split: shared-sync gets the SCRIPT into a repo and cannot wire it, because the plan stage lives in each repo's own deploy.yml alongside its runner label and working-directory -- see #1123 for the per-repo wiring, and be aware that a repo holding these two files is NOT thereby guarded. scripts/wait-for-checks.sh was added for #1154: every session hand-rolled its own `until ... gh pr checks ...` loop and the natural formulation polls for the ABSENCE of pending checks, which reads the empty window right after `gh pr update-branch` as 'all green' and merges a PR whose CI has not started. It qualifies as verbatim content because it takes the PR number and repo as arguments and reads branch protection for the repo it is pointed at -- nothing in it knows a layout. It needs only `gh`, using gh's embedded jq rather than a jq binary, so it runs anywhere `gh` is authenticated.
filesIfPresentNote: Files kept in step ONLY in repos that already hold them -- never created. Mapping is `target path in the satellite` -> `canonical copy in this repo`, because unlike `files` the two are not the same path: a sibling's apps/frontend/... has no counterpart at this repo's root (there is apps/portal/ and no apps/frontend/), so the skeleton IS the canonical copy. Added for #1107: `handleResponse` threw the entire response body as the error message, so a user saw `{"detail":"Administrator access required"}` where a page's content belonged. The identical function was in the skeleton and in all seven siblings, and `files` could not carry it: it CREATES what is absent, so it would have written a frontend API client into two plugin repos, two runner repos and a design repo that have no frontend at all -- and shared-files-parity.test.ts requires every `files` entry in EVERY skeleton, which apps/frontend/... can never satisfy in plugin-template. The mechanism can still backfill, deliberately: that is what `files` is for. This list is how you say a file must not be created, only kept current -- because putting a file into a repo that never had one is a decision somebody should make, not a side effect of adding a line to a manifest. Reconciling a file first is part of the price of entry: apps/frontend/src/lib/auth.ts is present in all seven siblings and diverges by 29-247 lines, so a one-way overwrite would clobber whichever behaviour is correct -- see #1117 before adding it.
filesFromSkeletonNote: The third list, added for #1150: files whose canonical copy lives in the SKELETON that matches the receiving repo's flavour, keyed to the policy for a repo that already holds one. Added because eleven of seventeen estate repos held NEITHER `AGENTS.md` NOR `CLAUDE.md` -- not a stale copy, nothing -- so an agent opening `tabsii-crm` got no worktree discipline, no honest-push rule, no never-merge-red and no reproduce-before-fixing. `files` creates but cannot remap a path, and the satellite ruleset is emphatically NOT this repo's root `AGENTS.md` (that one carries section 9 distribution, `core-manifest.json` and the upgrade flow, none of which applies to a satellite). `filesIfPresent` remaps but deliberately never creates, which is the one thing a backfill must do. Why this is a third list rather than `files` learning the `target -> source` map form, which was the cheaper-looking option: (1) THE SOURCE IS NOT ONE FILE. `_skeletons/plugin-template/AGENTS.md` legitimately differs from `_skeletons/sibling-template/AGENTS.md` by 50 lines -- the birth-time branch-protection and runner-grant checklist from #714, which exists because both plugin repos once ran with no branch protection at all. A single-source map would either delete that from the plugin repos or force it into every sibling, and `shared-files-parity.test.ts` would fail either way, since it requires every `files` entry byte-identical in EVERY skeleton and these two must not be. So the source is resolved per repo from its marker via `skeletonForMarker`. (2) THE TWO FILES NEED OPPOSITE POLICIES ON AN EXISTING COPY. `AGENTS.md` must be kept in step -- it drifting 68 lines behind in tabsii is #559, the founding injury of this whole mechanism -- so it is `sync`. `CLAUDE.md` must not be: its load-bearing content is the `@AGENTS.md` import, but it also carries a per-repo `What this repo is` paragraph, and four of the repos being backfilled (`biffo-runners`, `tabsii-runners`, `tabsii-map`, `tabsii-data-model-design`) are not sibling apps at all, so a one-way overwrite would assert in each of them that they are `a Biffo sibling app (ADR-0007)` whose identity lives in a `biffo.sibling.json` they do not have. `seed` means create where absent and never touch again; `--check` therefore reports a `seed` entry only when it is MISSING, because a differing copy is the repo exercising the ownership `seed` grants it. Repos with no marker (`biffo-runners`, `tabsii-runners`, `tabsii-map`, `tabsii-data-model-design`, in scope via the `scripts/verify.sh` clause) fall back to `skeletonDefault`. That is correct for `AGENTS.md`: the satellite ruleset is dev-branch, worktrees, Conventional Commits, PRs, never-merge-red, honest pushes and security -- it contains NO deploy clause, so there is nothing in it a repo without a deploy would need trimmed, and a trimmed variant would be a second document differing from the first by zero rules. `idea-corpus` is deliberately absent from all of this: it has no git remote, no `dev`, no CI and no branch protection, so every rule in the document would be unsatisfiable there and an agent's first act would be to flag a non-issue -- it needs a remote and a `dev` branch before it can carry the estate ruleset at all.
mustBeUniformNote: RECONCILED 2026-08-03 (#1117, #1190): auth.ts moved from 6 variants across 7 repos to 2, and auth.test.ts from 5 to 2, so both baselines were lowered from 6/5 to 2. The remaining two variants are (a) the sibling skeleton's copy, now byte-identical in six repos, and (b) tabsii-marketplace. THE BASELINE IS 2, NOT 1, ON PURPOSE and it should not be driven to 1 by overwriting marketplace: that repo genuinely exports signIn/signUp/confirmSignUp/signOut behind a PUBLIC self-service registration flow (/signin, /register, /register/buyer), and a one-way overwrite would delete the feature -- the exact failure the superset rule below warns about. Note also that auth.ts CANNOT be promoted to `filesIfPresent` while that is true: filesIfPresent is a one-way overwrite with no per-repo exclusion, so listing it would clobber marketplace on the next sync. The route to a baseline of 1, if anyone wants it, is to extract marketplace's registration mechanics into their own module (the same seam principle that puts per-app policy in auth-gate.tsx) and only then list the path -- not to widen the shared copy. What got the other six to identical was #1190 (runtime identity resolution reached 2 of 7 repos, credential pruning 1 of 7) plus removing dead signIn/signOut exports from geo and intake that nothing called. The fourth list, added for #1108: `path -> baseline variant count`. It asserts that a path should read IDENTICALLY across every repo that holds it, and unlike the three lists above it never writes anything -- scripts/shared-sync.sh only measures it and reports. This is deliberately not `files` or `filesIfPresent`, both of which are one-way overwrites: a shared-shaped file that has already diverged has NO channel to record that fact short of overwriting it, and overwriting is exactly wrong when nobody has yet established which copy's behaviour is correct. `_extract_detail` is why this exists -- it was written twice, independently, in two different siblings, fixing the same bug, because the second author had no way to discover the first had already solved it (#1107, closed; the class issue is #1108). A path in this list is a declaration that the debt is real and TRACKED, which has to happen before it can be paid down. `--check` fails a path only when its LIVE variant count exceeds the baseline recorded here -- copying the posture `biffo.orphan-baseline.json` established for the core-upgrade orphan ratchet (cli/src/lib/core-upgrade.ts, `checkOrphanRatchet`): pre-existing residue never hard-blocks, only a NEW regression does, because a guard that is red on the pre-existing set every morning is one people learn to scroll past (scripts/protection-audit.sh argues this at length, and scripts/shared-sync.sh --check feeds exactly that daily dashboard, scripts/practices-daily.sh line ~355). A path whose variants drop below its baseline is reported as improved and told to lower the baseline -- a ratchet that never tightens is a ratchet that stops meaning anything. Every measurement reads `origin/<base>` via `git ls-tree`/`git rev-parse`, NEVER a working tree: the first pass at this measured api-client.ts at 4 variants from working trees and 1 from remote refs, because the difference was a stale `git pull` on the machine doing the measuring, not anything in the estate -- a guard that fails on somebody's stale checkout is a fail-closed nuisance that trains people to ignore it. Only repos that actually hold a path count toward its holder/variant totals; a repo missing it entirely is not a failure -- that absence is what `files`/`filesIfPresent` exist to fix, not this list's job -- and an entry needs at least 2 holders to mean anything at all. Baselines below were measured 2026-08-02 from every in-scope repo's `origin/dev`. `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth.ts` (6 variants / 7 repos, #1117) is declared on SECURITY grounds, not merely because it differs: seven divergent authentication implementations are seven surfaces to audit independently, and the file's job is entirely plumbing -- Cognito pool resolution, session retrieval, credential hygiene, sign-in/out mechanics -- with NO app-specific policy in it (grepped all seven copies for `cognito:groups`/`groups`/`role`: zero hits in any of them). There is no category of legitimate per-app difference for this file to hold, which is why it belongs here rather than beside it in judgement calls about what counts as drift. Per-app variation belongs in `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth-gate.tsx` instead (present in 3 of 7 siblings, deliberately NOT in this list -- it is exactly where apps are meant to differ, gating which Cognito groups an app admits, and declaring it here would be the opposite error). The divergence itself is the `_extract_detail` pattern recurring in the file this is named for: `cognito-hygiene.ts` (added for #834, after `dev.biffo.io` was measured carrying four Cognito pools' credentials, three of them dead) reached only 1 of 7 siblings; `identity.ts` (the #403 runtime-identity mechanism, letting a pool resolve from a runtime identity document rather than a build-time env var) reached only 2 of 7. Two template-side security fixes, each stuck in the repo(s) that happened to receive them, because nothing said 'this shape already exists elsewhere, go look' -- happening in the security-critical file, while this issue was being written. Convergence must target the SUPERSET of exports, never the intersection: four repos export only `getCurrentSession`; `tabsii-geo`/`tabsii-intake` (byte-identical to each other) add `signIn`/`completeNewPassword`/`signOut`; `tabsii-marketplace` adds `signUp`/`confirmSignUp` for public self-service registration. A future reconciliation that picks the smallest copy as canonical would delete marketplace's registration feature outright -- the canonical module must carry the full function set, with each sibling importing only what it uses (unused exports tree-shake, so carrying the superset costs nothing). `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth.test.ts` (5 variants / 6 repos) is auth.ts's companion test file and tracked for the same reason -- a test suite that diverges from its module's real shape is verifying six different fictions. `services/api/src/api/core_client.py` (4 variants / 7 repos) is where `_extract_detail` itself was written twice; #1107 fixed the bug in two siblings, and this entry is how the other five stop being invisible. Deliberately NOT seeded: `services/api/src/api/main.py` (6 variants / 7 repos) -- a sibling's API entrypoint mounts its own routers, so it plausibly differs by design in a way auth.ts's plumbing does not; the omission is a decision, not an oversight, and a future measurement is welcome to make the case for tracking it once someone has actually read all seven and classified the differences (see 'Reconcile before you distribute' above).
supersedesNote: Raw commands each shared script replaces, checked by scripts/ci-wiring-audit.sh. shared-sync.sh gets the script INTO a repo; nothing made the repo call it, and on 2026-07-29 eleven repos merged the scripts and every one carried on running the raw command -- drift went to zero and the outcome did not move (#884). ci.yml cannot be a one-way overwrite because the path depends on that step's working-directory, so the mechanism is an assertion rather than a copy: you cannot write the line for the repo, but you can refuse to let it forget. Add a pair here whenever a shared script supersedes a command repos invoke directly; the check only fires in repos that actually hold the script, so a repo shared-sync has not reached yet is reported once, by shared-sync, rather than twice.
